audit_meta.honest_assessment: LaunchedIn10 is in deep authority-deficit stasis. 23 audits, 2 total clicks, 0 conversions, 0 AI citations this period. Three P0 issues (top page redirect collapse, soft 404s, price schema) are actively destroying existing equity and must be fixed. Everything else is a consequence of zero content velocity and zero authority investment for 7+ months. The site is correctly classified as maintenance-only — fix the P0s and leave it alone until investment resumes.

action_items.description: CRITICAL: The top impression page (/blog/website-design/7-companies-that-design-websites-for-small/) is being treated by Google as 'Page with redirect' with canonical collapsed to /blog/. This page generates 49% of all GSC impressions (4,295 of 8,743) and recorded the site's only organic click. Google last crawled it on 03.09.26 — nearly 2 months stale. The SPA catch-all rewrite rule in _redirects ('/* /index.html 200') is the likely cause: Cloudflare serves the SPA shell, and Google may interpret this as a redirect rather than a direct response. The SSG pre-renders static HTML for this URL via generate-static.js, but the _redirects rule may override it. This is the single highest-value content asset on the domain and it is effectively deindexed.
action_items.prompt:
Investigate and fix the redirect treatment of https://launchedin10.co.uk/blog/website-design/7-companies-that-design-websites-for-small/ on launchedin10.co.uk (repo: EldrisOU/launchedin10-final).

1. Read the _redirects file in the repo root or public/ directory. The SPA catch-all '/* /index.html 200' may be overriding the SSG pre-rendered HTML.
2. Check if dist/ contains a pre-rendered HTML file at the correct path after running 'npm run build'. If the SSG output exists but _redirects catches it first, Cloudflare serves the SPA shell instead.
3. Fix: Add an explicit rule ABOVE the catch-all for all blog post paths that have SSG output, e.g.:
   /blog/* /blog/:splat 200
   OR remove the catch-all and let Cloudflare Pages serve static files directly (which is the default CF Pages behaviour).
4. After fixing, verify by running: curl -sI https://launchedin10.co.uk/blog/website-design/7-companies-that-design-websites-for-small/ — should return 200 with the correct page title in the body, not a SPA shell.
5. Then use gsc_inspect_url to request re-indexing of this URL. Google should re-crawl and see the direct HTML response instead of a redirect.
6. Do NOT push to GitHub without operator authorisation.
action_items.verification: Run gsc_inspect_url on https://launchedin10.co.uk/blog/website-design/7-companies-that-design-websites-for-small/ — coverage state should change from 'Page with redirect' to 'Submitted and indexed' with self-referencing canonical within 7-14 days of fix deployment.
action_items.estimated_impact: Restores indexing for the page generating 49% of all GSC impressions (4,295). Potential to capture clicks from positions 25-35 on 'web design small business' query cluster.
action_items.evidence: GSC URL Inspection 29.10.26: coverage_state='Page with redirect', google_canonical='/blog/', last_crawled=03.09.26. curl returns HTTP 200 with full page content — Google is interpreting the _redirects rewrite as a redirect.

action_items.description: Two sale landing page URLs (/seo-automation-sale/ and /website-translation-sale/) return HTTP 200 but serve identical homepage content — same title, same H1, same canonical pointing to /. These are soft 404s. They are unknown to both Google and Bing (never crawled, never discovered). If these URLs appear in any internal links, old Google Ads campaigns, or external references, they cannibalise the homepage and waste crawl budget. The SPA catch-all rewrite rule serves the homepage React shell for any URL that doesn't have a pre-rendered SSG counterpart, which means these URLs were either never built as SSG pages or their SSG files were removed.
action_items.prompt:
Fix soft 404s on launchedin10.co.uk (repo: EldrisOU/launchedin10-final).

1. Check if /seo-automation-sale/ and /website-translation-sale/ have dedicated content in generate-static.js or any React route. If they do not have dedicated pages:
   a. Add 301 redirects in _redirects ABOVE the catch-all:
      /seo-automation-sale/ /seo-automation/ 301
      /website-translation-sale/ /website-translation/ 301
   b. This redirects visitors to the actual service pages with unique content.
2. Verify these URLs are NOT in sitemap.xml — check generate-sitemap.js output.
3. Search the entire codebase for any internal links pointing to these URLs and update them to the correct /seo-automation/ and /website-translation/ paths.
4. Do NOT push to GitHub without operator authorisation.
action_items.verification: curl -sI https://launchedin10.co.uk/seo-automation-sale/ — should return HTTP 301 to /seo-automation/. curl -sI https://launchedin10.co.uk/website-translation-sale/ — should return HTTP 301 to /website-translation/.
action_items.estimated_impact: Eliminates 2 soft 404s, prevents homepage cannibalisation, cleans crawl budget.
action_items.evidence: curl 29.10.26: both URLs return HTTP 200 with homepage title ('High-Performance Web Design in 10 Days'), homepage H1, canonical pointing to /. GSC: both 'URL is unknown to Google'. Bing Block A: /seo-automation-sale/ discovered=never, doc_size=0, IsPage=false.

action_items.description: Homepage JSON-LD Service schema prices do not match the visible HTML prices. This is the 8th consecutive audit flagging this issue. The homepage HTML body prominently displays SEO automation subscription prices (£99.95/mo, £149.95/mo, £195.00/mo) but the JSON-LD Service schema declares web design activation prices (£497, £997, £1,997) and monthly management fees (£99, £149, £249). Google may flag this as misleading structured data since the prices a user sees on the page do not correspond to the prices in the schema. The /pricing/ page has correctly aligned prices. Resolution requires an operator decision: either (a) move the Service schema from homepage to /pricing/ only, or (b) update the homepage Service schema to reflect SEO automation prices, or (c) restructure the homepage to show web design prices instead of SEO automation prices.
action_items.prompt:
Fix homepage JSON-LD Service schema price mismatch on launchedin10.co.uk (repo: EldrisOU/launchedin10-final).

OPERATOR DECISION REQUIRED — choose one:

Option A: Move Service schema to /pricing/ only
- In generate-static.js, remove the Service schema from the homepage injection
- The /pricing/ page already has correctly aligned Service schema
- Homepage keeps Organization, WebSite, WebPage, FAQPage, BreadcrumbList

Option B: Update homepage Service schema to SEO automation prices
- In generate-static.js, change the homepage Service schema offers to match the visible SEO automation prices: £99.95, £149.95, £195.00 monthly
- Update name/description to reflect SEO automation service

Option C: Change homepage HTML to show web design prices
- Replace the SEO automation pricing section on the homepage with web design activation pricing (£497/£997/£1,997)
- This aligns HTML with existing JSON-LD

Do NOT proceed without operator selecting Option A, B, or C.
action_items.verification: curl -sL https://launchedin10.co.uk/ | extract JSON-LD Service schema prices AND visible HTML currency values. All prices in JSON-LD must have matching visible prices on the page.
action_items.estimated_impact: Eliminates structured data policy violation risk. Prices in SERP rich results will match what users see on the page.
action_items.evidence: 8th consecutive audit. HTML: £99.95, £149.95, £195.00 (SEO automation). JSON-LD: £497, £997, £1,997, £99, £149, £249 (web design). /pricing/ page correctly aligned.

action_items.description: Google URL Inspection shows /pricing/ as 'Page with redirect' (canonical redirects to /) despite the page serving unique content with its own title ('Web Design & SEO Pricing | LaunchedIn10'), H1 ('Transparent Pricing'), and self-referencing canonical. This is the same SPA catch-all issue affecting ACT-LI10-055 — Cloudflare's _redirects rule may be causing Google to treat the response as a redirect. The /pricing/ page is fully indexed in Bing (26,341 bytes, last crawled 04.10.26) confirming the content exists and is crawlable. Google's redirect treatment means this page is not independently indexed, which explains 4 consecutive audits of '/pricing/ not indexed'. This supersedes ACT-LI10-050.
action_items.prompt:
Fix /pricing/ redirect treatment on launchedin10.co.uk (repo: EldrisOU/launchedin10-final).

This is related to ACT-LI10-055 — same root cause (_redirects SPA catch-all).

1. When fixing _redirects for ACT-LI10-055, also ensure /pricing/ is served directly as SSG HTML, not through the SPA rewrite.
2. Add an explicit rule: /pricing/ /pricing/index.html 200 (or ensure CF Pages serves the pre-rendered file directly).
3. After deployment, use gsc_inspect_url to request re-indexing of https://launchedin10.co.uk/pricing/.
4. Do NOT push to GitHub without operator authorisation.
action_items.verification: Run gsc_inspect_url on https://launchedin10.co.uk/pricing/ — coverage state should change from 'Page with redirect' to 'Submitted and indexed' with self-referencing canonical.
action_items.estimated_impact: Restores Google indexing for the pricing page. Bing already has it indexed (26KB). Resolves 4-audit-old ACT-LI10-050.
action_items.evidence: GSC URL Inspection 29.10.26: 'Page with redirect', canonical=/, last crawled 12.10.26. curl returns HTTP 200 with unique content (title: 'Web Design & SEO Pricing'). Bing Block A: IsPage=true, doc_size=26,341, last_crawled=04.10.26.

action_items.description: The global stylesheet src/index.css contains an unscoped attribute selector '[data-ai-summary]' with !important that hides any element carrying the data-ai-summary attribute. This is the exact same pattern that caused the torxup.co.uk incident (ACT-TORX-038, 15.06.26 — 04.08.26) where 35 URLs rendered blank for 7 weeks. Currently benign on LI10 because all existing data-ai-summary elements are purpose-built summary divs containing only summary text. However, any future addition of the attribute to a content wrapper (e.g. a page body div, an h1, a lede paragraph) would immediately hide the entire page. The RS-5 rule requires scoping this selector to the purpose-built element class. Allow-list: ONLY div.aeo-summary elements may carry data-ai-summary.
action_items.verification: RS-4 render check: node rs4-check.js on all commercial pages + blog index. Must return exit 0 with [] violations. Then curl each page and confirm data-ai-summary elements still render as 1x1px hidden (not visible, but also not hiding any content-bearing parent).
action_items.estimated_impact: Prevents future render catastrophe. Does not change current visual appearance.
action_items.evidence: src/index.css contains unscoped [data-ai-summary] { ... !important }. Same pattern as torxup ACT-TORX-038 (35 URLs blank for 7 weeks). RS-5 pre-flight detected in Step -1.

action_items.description: All pages share the same dateModified value (build timestamp from generate-static.js) rather than actual content modification dates. This means Google sees all 118 pages as modified on the same date — the last build. Currently not impactful because the site hasn't been rebuilt in 3+ months anyway. 5th consecutive audit. Becomes relevant only when content velocity resumes.
action_items.prompt: MONITOR ONLY — no action required until content publishing resumes. When LI10 returns to active development, modify generate-static.js to use each post's Supabase updated_at timestamp for dateModified instead of the build date.
